subject: Clarifying Redwood default visibility and purge pathways for EU prospect
messages:
From: Alice Grant <security@brightbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <devops@brightbank.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on default retention for requests & outputs (EU)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Before we proceed with an eval, our security and compliance teams want a clear write-up of Redwood's default data retention and deletion behavior for EU customers. Specifically:

- By default how long are raw requests (prompts) and generated outputs stored?
- Are streaming fragments treated differently from completed responses?
- Where are those logs physically stored for EU tenants (region/residency)?
- What is the standard procedure and SLA to process a customer-initiated deletion / DSR?
- Do you retain any aggregated telemetry beyond the customer-visible retention window? If so, is it ever used to reconstruct content?

We need something concise we can pass to our privacy team. Also any SOC2 / audit evidence pointers would help.

Thanks,
Alice Grant
Head of Security, BrightBank
security@brightbank.com

(attachment: brightbank-eval-questions.xlsx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
To: Alice Grant <security@brightbank.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <devops@brightbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention for requests & outputs (EU)

Hi Alice — great questions, thanks for outlining them. I'm looping in Marissa from Product/Privacy so we can give an authoritative response and include the audit artifacts you asked for. A few quick, high-level points while we assemble the full write-up: 

- Default capture: by default Redwood retains request and response artifacts in the hot store for 30 days. After 30 days, artifacts move to a limited cold tier; content is retained in the cold tier only for forensic/debugging purposes unless the customer has opted-in to extended retention.
- Streaming: streaming fragments are captured as part of the same request record; we do not persist interim chunks separately beyond the parent request record.
- Residency: for customers with EU residency enabled, data is kept within EU regions and backups follow the same residency contract.
- Deletion/DSR: customers can file a deletion request via the privacy portal or by opening a ticket; we acknowledge within 48 hours and target completion within 30 days unless there are legal holds.
- Aggregated telemetry: we keep aggregated, non-reconstructable telemetry for product health (token volumes, latency histograms) by default; this data cannot be used to reconstruct prompts/outputs.

I'll attach a short summary and the SOC2 artifact pointers — Marissa, can you confirm the wording and add any necessary caveats for EU-regulated customers?

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
(attachment: retention-summary-brightbank.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Alice Grant <security@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@sean_gallagher@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T13:26:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention for requests & outputs (EU)

Hi — tagging in details from Privacy & Prod. A few clarifications to Vanessa's summary so BrightBank can pass these straight to legal/privacy: 

1) Definition: for this thread "requests/prompts" = the client payload sent to the API (text, metadata like model/version, and request headers when explicitly captured). "Outputs" = model-generated tokens, streaming and completed outputs.

2) Default retention windows (EU residency flag enabled):
   - Hot store (full fidelity): 30 days. Accessible to support/ops under guarded workflows for debugging and incident response.
   - Cold tier (limited access, forensic only): up to 540 days by default for internal investigation — however, content is encrypted at rest and access is audited. Customers can contract shorter windows.

3) Streaming behavior: streaming data is attached to the parent request record and not separately indexed. If a customer requests deletion, the entire parent record (including any stream fragments) is removed per the deletion SLA.

4) Deletion / DSR process: submit a DSR via the data-requests portal or email privacy@redwood.example.com. We issue an acknowledgement within 48 hours. Standard completion target is 30 days; for EU customers we aim to complete within 14 days where the residency flag is set and there are no legal holds.

5) Aggregate telemetry: retained indefinitely in an anonymized form (no text-level reconstruction). Any telemetry surfaced in dashboards is aggregated; raw token text is not stored in telemetry buckets.

6) Edge cases:
   - Customer-managed keys: if the customer uses a KMS and requests deletion, we still remove service-layer copies; key revocation may leave ciphertext in backups until key rotation/retention completes — we'll coordinate with customer security.
   - Legal holds: we will not purge records subject to a lawful preservation demand.

I've attached a short PDF tailored for prospect Q&A and a link to the EU deletion runbook (internal). Happy to redline if BrightBank prefers stricter defaults.

- Marissa
Director, Product Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-eu-retention-brief.pdf)

On the runbook link: https://drive.redwood.example.com/teams/privacy/runbooks/eu-deletion-runbook

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Alice Grant <security@brightbank.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention for requests & outputs (EU)

Adding a few operational points from Privacy/Legal for BrightBank's checklist: 

- DSR scope: when a deletion request targets an identifier (account id, API key), we locate all related request/response records and tombstone them. Tombstoned records enter a purge queue; purge is irreversible once completed.

- SLA nuance: 14-day target for EU-residency customers is our internal goal; exceptions: (a) ongoing investigations, (b) legal hold, or (c) customer requests requiring cross-region co-ordination. We communicate expected completion time in the initial 48-hour acknowledgement.

- Reconstructability: cold-tier forensic copies are encrypted and access-controlled; engineering guarantees that aggregated telemetry cannot be reverse-engineered into prompt or output text. We have a documented review process for any forensic access requests.

- API-driven delete: customers can call the Data Deletion endpoint (POST /v1/customers/{id}/delete) with signed tokens; we return a job id and progress endpoint. We also support manual DSRs initiated via privacy@redwood.example.com for customers without automation.

I'll attach the DSR template for BrightBank to start with.

-Karthik
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference
(attachment: dsr-request-form.docx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2028-06-05T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on default retention for requests & outputs (EU)

Alice — thanks again for the list. Summary for your docs team (ready to send onward):

- Default retention (EU residency enabled): 30 days hot (full fidelity), then move to limited cold tier. Default cold retention for internal forensic use: up to 540 days; customers can negotiate a shorter cold horizon on contract.
- Streaming: fragments are part of the parent request record and removed when that record is purged.
- Residency: EU-enabled tenants keep data inside EU regions and backups follow residency controls.
- Deletion/DSR: acknowledge 48 hours, standard completion target 14 days for EU-residency accounts (30 days in exceptional cases). Deletion is irreversible after purge.
- Aggregated telemetry: retained in anonymized/aggregated form; cannot be used to reconstruct customer text.

I attached a short one-pager tailored for BrightBank and the DSR template — happy to walk your privacy/legal team through it if helpful. If this looks good I'll send the PDF as an official record and include the SOC2 evidence pointers we discussed in the demo.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
